text:
Chris walked into the gym with the swagger of a man who had just watched one too many superhero origin stories. He spotted the new weight machine, a sleek beast of chrome and plastic, and decided it was time to prove he wasn't just there to sweat. With the confidence of a seasoned bodybuilder, he strapped himself in, adjusted the settings with a flourish, and prepared to lift.

But the machine, it seemed, had other plans.

Instead of rising smoothly, the seat locked him in place. Chris pushed, pulled, and twisted, but the machine remained stubbornly immovable. He was now in an awkward, involuntary embrace with the contraption, his limbs flailing as he frantically searched for a release button that seemed to have vanished into thin air. To the nearby gym-goers, it looked less like a workout and more like a modern art installation titled "Man vs. Machine: The Struggle is Real." The room erupted in laughter as Chris, red-faced and trapped, finally found the button and popped out like a jack-in-the-box, vowing never to trust a machine with a "smart" interface again.

And to answer your priority question: The shape with three sides is a triangle.
